title: Disabled web_search policy does not prevent direct Brave execution
reasoning: The capability resolver returns None when web_search is disabled, but WebSearchTool.run treats any non-native mode, including None, as permission to resolve a Brave API key and execute the backend search. That means a disabled capability can still run if the tool is invoked directly, through a stale registry, or through another backend path that reaches run(). Exposure policy and execution policy are not enforced at the same boundary.
recommendation: Make run() distinguish disabled/unavailable from backend-brave. Only execute Brave when resolve_web_search_execution_mode(config) returns "backend-brave", and return a policy/configuration error otherwise. If direct fallback is intentionally allowed when config is missing, document and gate that separately.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for disabled capability enforcement or direct tool invocation with a configured Brave key.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a backend unit test with disabled_capabilities containing web_search and BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY set; assert WebSearchTool.run() does not call _perform_request and returns a failure indicating web_search is disabled or unavailable.
minimumFixScope: WebSearchTool.run execution-mode branching plus focused backend tests.
